rows.phenotypeRestriction: established bronchiectasis with separately diagnosed obstructive sleep apnea
rows.sourceTitle: Obstructive Sleep Apnea in Bronchiectasis: Prevalence, Risk Factors and Clinical Implications-A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
rows.citation: Srivali N, De Giacomi F. Obstructive Sleep Apnea in Bronchiectasis: Prevalence, Risk Factors and Clinical Implications-A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis. J Sleep Res. 2026;35(4):e70333. PMID 41905893. doi:10.1111/jsr.70333.
rows.proposition: In adults with established bronchiectasis, polysomnography-confirmed obstructive sleep apnea is substantially more prevalent than in the general population; this supports screening and a population-level association only.
rows.publicationGuard: Do not infer obstructive sleep apnea from bronchiectasis alone. Require a separate obstructive sleep apnea diagnosis. Preserve obesity, craniofacial or anatomic upper-airway factors, age, sex, medication exposure, other sleep-disordered-breathing causes, and conventional obstructive sleep apnea risk factors. Association evidence must not be presented as individual causation.

rows.phenotypeRestriction: autoimmune thyroiditis only, with separately established chronic urticaria
rows.sourceTitle: Effects of Treatment with L-Thyroxine on Chronic Urticaria in Subjects with Autoimmune Thyroiditis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
rows.citation: Bordoni M, Ciarloni A, Aboud N, Sidori E, Silvetti F, Taccaliti A, Vassallo A, Romeo M, Salvio G, Balercia G. Effects of Treatment with L-Thyroxine on Chronic Urticaria in Subjects with Autoimmune Thyroiditis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis. Int J Mol Sci. 2026;27(14):6348. PMID 42511690. doi:10.3390/ijms27146348.
rows.proposition: Chronic urticaria is frequently associated with autoimmune thyroiditis, while pathogenesis and the benefit of thyroid-directed treatment remain uncertain; this evidence supports association only.
rows.publicationGuard: Require autoimmune thyroiditis and chronic urticaria to be independently established. Do not generalize from nonspecific thyroiditis, do not infer that autoimmune thyroiditis individually causes urticaria, and do not use levothyroxine response as proof of causation.

rows.phenotypeRestriction: Charcot neuroarthropathy of the foot, especially neuropathic or diabetic Charcot foot, with a separately established osteomyelitis diagnosis
rows.sourceTitle: Pharmacological treatment for Charcot neuroarthropathy: a systematic review
rows.citation: Liu L, Lu J, Wang J, Wang Q, Zhao H, Zhang Y. Pharmacological treatment for Charcot neuroarthropathy: a systematic review. BMC Musculoskelet Disord. 2026;27(1):592. PMID 42141385. doi:10.1186/s12891-026-09965-w.
rows.proposition: Charcot neuroarthropathy can progress to foot deformity and ulceration, creating a clinically recognized pathway to deep infection and osteomyelitis; use of this relationship requires documented wound or infection chronology.
rows.publicationGuard: Require established Charcot neuroarthropathy of the foot plus documented deformity with ulceration, soft-tissue breakdown, wound infection, or compatible deep-infection chronology before using the osteomyelitis pathway. Osteomyelitis must be separately diagnosed. Preserve diabetes, neuropathy, peripheral vascular disease, trauma or surgery, wound-care history, and other infection risk factors.

rows.phenotypeRestriction: established Lyme disease or Lyme borreliosis context with separately diagnosed uveitis
rows.sourceTitle: Ocular findings in patients with lyme disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis
rows.citation: Barbosa LIT, Lima RV, Moreira JLML, Hira S, Arruda MP, Zinher MT, Thomaz S, Del Valle GS. Ocular findings in patients with lyme disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Graefes Arch Clin Exp Ophthalmol. 2026;264(4):1101-1110. PMID 41546697. doi:10.1007/s00417-025-07110-2.
rows.proposition: Uveitis, including anterior, intermediate and posterior forms, is among documented ocular manifestations reported in patients with Lyme disease.
rows.publicationGuard: Require Lyme disease or Lyme borreliosis and uveitis to be independently established. Preserve other infectious, autoimmune, medication-related, traumatic, and ophthalmic etiologies. Population-level manifestation evidence does not by itself establish an individual nexus.

rows.phenotypeRestriction: established narcolepsy with separately diagnosed hypertension; association appears strongest in narcolepsy type 1
rows.sourceTitle: Narcolepsy and metabolic disease: A meta-analytic synthesis
rows.citation: Zhang X, Yin W, Ren J, Zhou X, Zha M, Zong Q, Shen Y, Spruyt K, Zhou J. Narcolepsy and metabolic disease: A meta-analytic synthesis. Sleep Med Rev. 2026;87:102264. PMID 41747645. doi:10.1016/j.smrv.2026.102264.
rows.proposition: Hypertension is among the cardiometabolic comorbidities reported in narcolepsy, with greater cardiometabolic burden particularly in narcolepsy type 1; this supports association and screening relevance only.
rows.publicationGuard: Require separately diagnosed hypertension. Preserve obesity, obstructive sleep apnea, metabolic syndrome, stimulant or other medication exposure, age, sex, renal or endocrine causes, and other conventional hypertension risk factors. Do not state or imply individual causation from the meta-analysis alone.
